life is always about saving yourself ; it 's not about healing others . only once you 're in a good place you can offer help . only once the other person is in a good place they will accept it .

“ one last conversation ” does n't inherently mean you 're trying to fix someone , it can simply be about saying the words you 've always needed to say , with no attachment to a particular outcome . it also is n't an “ either or ” to the deeper emotional work that 's useful for healing .

1/2 there 's a vast difference between telling your plan to end a relationship with someone so toxic that doing so cd literally be dangerous , vs telling your truth in a way that sets healthy boundaries for yourself .

overcoming my fear and telling the truth about why i was ending relationships has been * tremendously * empowering for me , vs just ghosting or leaving w / o telling my truth , which only perpetuated me feeling like a scared victim . i 'm not saying that 's for everybody though .

i also think the term toxic is over used and sometimes misappropriated . we live in a time when , i think , we want to oversimplify and take the easiest way out . in the process , we may dehumanize people . what 's appropriate treatment for abusers may be deeply harmful to others .
